body: When Boeing designed the 787 Dreamliner in the early 2000s, its engineers shifted the design baseline toward human physiology: long-haul travel strains the body through jet lag, dehydration and high-altitude fatigue, and advanced materials and systems could actively mitigate those effects. The result is a cabin altitude of approximately 6,000 feet, a maximum pressure differential of 9.06 pounds per square inch, relative humidity of up to 25%, and windows 65% larger than industry standards.

On conventional aluminum airframes, maximum cabin altitude at a typical cruising altitude of 40,000 feet is capped at approximately 8,000 feet. A study published in the New England Journal of Medicine found that after three to nine hours at a simulated cabin altitude of 8,000 feet, blood oxygen saturation dropped by an average of 4.4 percentage points, triggering headaches, cognitive sluggishness and muscle aches. The 787 sustains the higher pressure differential with carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites, which make up roughly 50% of its airframe by weight, including the main fuselage barrel sections.

Humidity and windows are equally central to the design. Conventional jets supply cabin air with engine bleed air and restrict humidity to under 10% to avoid condensation corrosion, while the 787's bleedless design uses electrically driven compressors to draw fresh outside air directly into the environmental control system, and its composite airframe allows active humidifiers. Its windows measure 10.7 by 18.4 inches and use Gentex electrochromic dimming across five opacity levels, blocking over 99.99% of visible light and thermal infrared energy in their darkest setting.

Ride smoothness comes from Smooth Ride Technology: pressure sensors in the nose detect incoming vertical gusts milliseconds before they strike the lifting surfaces, and the flight control computers calculate counteracting control surface adjustments, while the flexible carbon wings absorb gust energy. The counterweight is seat width: the 787's cabin cross-section of roughly 215 inches was designed around an 8-abreast, 2-4-2 layout with seats about 18.5 inches wide, but most operators chose a 9-abreast, 3-3-3 layout that narrows seats to between 17.0 and 17.3 inches, while the A350 XWB's 221-inch cross-section still accommodates 18-inch seats in a 9-abreast layout.
en.summary: The Boeing 787 pairs a roughly 6,000-foot cabin altitude, humidity of up to 25% and windows 65% larger than standard with a trade-off: nine-abreast economy seating narrows seat width.
en.title: The hidden math behind the Boeing 787's legendary long-haul passenger experience

facts.claim: The Boeing 787's passenger experience is defined by a 6,000-foot cabin altitude, a 9.06 psi pressure differential, humidity of up to 25%, and windows 65% larger than industry standards.

On conventional aluminum airframes such as the 767 or A330, maximum cabin altitude at 40,000 feet is capped at approximately 8,000 feet, and a New England Journal of Medicine study found blood oxygen saturation dropped by an average of 4.4 percentage points after three to nine hours at a simulated 8,000-foot cabin altitude.
The 787 uses carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites for roughly 50% of its airframe by weight, including the main fuselage barrel sections, to withstand the higher pressure differential.

The 787's bleedless design uses electrically driven compressors to draw fresh outside air into the environmental control system, and its composite airframe allows active humidifiers to push relative humidity up to 15% to 25%.

The 787's windows measure 10.7 by 18.4 inches, use Gentex electrochromic dimming across five opacity levels, and block over 99.99% of visible light and thermal infrared energy in their darkest setting.

The 787's cabin cross-section of roughly 215 inches was designed for an 8-abreast 2-4-2 layout with seats about 18.5 inches wide, while a 9-abreast 3-3-3 layout narrows seats to 17.0 to 17.3 inches, compared with the A350 XWB's 221-inch cross-section accommodating 18-inch seats in a 9-abreast layout.

body: 波音在2000年代初期設計787夢幻客機時，把設計重心從單純的航程與燃油效率，轉向人體生理：長程飛行會造成時差、脫水與高空疲勞，工程團隊希望以先進材料與系統主動減輕這些負擔。結果是約6000英尺的客艙高度、9.06磅／平方英寸的最大壓差、最高25%的相對濕度，以及比業界標準大65%的窗戶。
傳統鋁合金機身在約40000英尺巡航高度時，客艙高度上限約為8000英尺；一篇刊於新英格蘭醫學期刊的研究發現，在模擬8000英尺客艙高度3至9小時後，受試者血氧飽和度平均下降4.4個百分點，進而引發頭痛、反應遲緩與肌肉痠痛。787以碳纖維複合材料承受較高的壓差，碳纖維複合材料約占機身重量50%，包括主要機身筒段，因此能在不超出結構疲勞限制的情況下維持較低的客艙高度。
濕度與窗戶同樣是這套設計的關鍵：傳統客機以發動機引氣供氣，為避免冷凝腐蝕而把客艙濕度限制在10%以下；787改用無引氣設計，以電動壓縮機直接吸入外界新鮮空氣，複合材料機身不怕鏽蝕，因此可配備主動加濕器。窗戶尺寸為10.7乘18.4英寸，採用Gentex電致變色調光技術，分5段不透明度調整，最暗狀態可阻擋超過99.99%的可見光與熱紅外線能量。

飛行平穩度則來自Smooth Ride Technology：機頭的壓力感測器可在垂直陣風撞擊升力面前數毫秒偵測到它，飛控電腦隨即計算反制動作，配合高展弦比碳纖維機翼的彈性吸震，讓顛簸化為低振幅的起伏。不過座椅寬度是這套舒適方程式的反向力量：787客艙截面約215英寸，原設計為8排2-4-2布局、座椅寬約18.5英寸，但多數航空公司改採9排3-3-3布局後，座椅寬度縮減至17.0至17.3英寸，相較之下A350XWB的221英寸截面在9排布局下仍可維持18英寸座椅寬度。
zh.summary: 波音787以約6000英尺的客艙高度、最高25%的相對濕度與大65%的窗戶，重新定義長程飛行的舒適標準，但9排經濟艙座椅寬度卻抵銷了部分優勢。
zh.title: 波音787長程客艙體驗背後的隱藏數學
